en.headline: M+ surveys two centuries of Asian fantasy art until next April
en.dek: More than 400 works fill the West Kowloon museum’s special exhibition on myths, monsters and popular culture, open since mid-October.
body: The M+ museum in the West Kowloon Cultural District is presenting Myths and Monsters: The Art of Fantasy in Asia, a special exhibition that opened to the public on 17 October and runs until 4 April 2027.

According to the museum, the show is the first major survey tracing how artists across Asia have used fantasy to respond to their times, from the nineteenth century to the present. It brings together more than 400 works spanning visual art, architecture, fashion, video games and moving images, arranged in four sections that begin with premodern traditions such as Japanese woodblock prints, Chinese shadow puppets and Tibetan Buddhist scrolls.

A newly commissioned site-specific mural by Hong Kong-born artist Oscar Chan Yik Long, titled Fear Catcher, draws on the figure of Zhong Kui from Chinese mythology. Admission is HK$190 for adults and HK$100 for concessions; a single ticket covers all M+ exhibitions. The museum is open from 10am to 6pm Tuesday to Thursday and at weekends, and until 10pm on Fridays, and is closed on Mondays except for special arrangements.

zh.headline: M+「神話與怪獸」展出逾400件亞洲奇幻作品 展期至明年四月
zh.dek: 西九文化區博物館特別展覽自十月中開放，涵蓋十九至二十一世紀神話、怪獸及流行文化。
body: 西九文化區M+博物館正展出特別展覽「神話與怪獸：亞洲的奇幻異境」，展覽於10月17日向公眾開放，展期至2027年4月4日。
博物館表示，這是首個大型專題展，追溯亞洲藝術家如何以奇幻回應所處時代，內容橫跨十九至二十一世紀。展品超過400件，涵蓋視覺藝術、建築、時尚、電子遊戲及動態影像，分四個章節呈現，由日本浮世繪、中國皮影戲及西藏唐卡等前現代傳統開始。
香港出生藝術家陳翊朗獲委託創作場地特定壁畫「Fear Catcher」，取材中國神話中的鍾庆形象。成人門票190港元，特惠100港元，一張門票可參觀M+所有展覽。博物館星期二至四及周末上午10時至下午6時開放，星期五延至晚上10時，星期一休館，特別安排除外。
